title: VM, container, microVM or function?

rows.label: You manage
values: The OS and everything above it
Your image; the host OS is shared
A small kernel and root filesystem, or nothing on a platform built on them
Only the handler code

rows.label: Isolation
values: Own kernel, hardware virtualisation
Shared host kernel; a kernel bug can cross the boundary
Own kernel, hardware virtualisation
Whatever the platform uses; Lambda uses microVMs

rows.label: Start-up time
values: Tens of seconds to minutes
Seconds or less
About 125 ms to boot; less from a snapshot
Milliseconds warm; up to seconds cold

rows.label: You pay for
values: Every second it runs
The machines it runs on, or per task
Usually per second of runtime, through a platform built on them
Each request and millisecond of runtime

rows.label: Longest single run
values: Unlimited
Unlimited
Unlimited
Capped, e.g. 15 minutes on Lambda

rows.label: Cost when idle
values: Full price
Depends; some platforms scale to zero
Low; platforms suspend or snapshot idle microVMs and charge only for stored state
Zero

rows.label: Reach for it for
values: Legacy apps, special OS needs, full control
Services that must run the same everywhere
Running untrusted or multi-tenant code safely
Event-driven glue and spiky, short tasks

tip: These layer on each other more than they compete: containers usually run on VMs, and function platforms run your code inside containers or microVMs. The real questions are how much of the stack you want to own, and whether you trust the code you’re running.
